misconceptions.description: Treating highlighting interesting lines as transcript annotation, with no defined code scheme another rater could reproduce
misconceptions.trigger: learner marks lines as 'good thinking' without a defined code or warrant
misconceptions.feedback: Define a small code scheme (for example claim, question, reasoning) and write a warrant for each code so another rater could reproduce your annotation.

misconceptions.description: Tagging a turn with a code but not stating the evidence in the turn that justifies the code
misconceptions.trigger: learner labels a turn 'reasoning' but does not quote or paraphrase what changed
misconceptions.feedback: Beside each code, write the warrant: the specific phrase or move in that turn that justifies the label.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a personal annotation is valid without checking whether another teacher would code the same turns the same way
misconceptions.trigger: learner never asks whether the codes are reproducible by a colleague
misconceptions.feedback: Check inter-rater agreement. If a colleague using your scheme would code differently, tighten the code definitions.
